title: Routing authoring grid: region/tier selector and fallback matrix with safety checks
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Provide a customer-facing routing policy authoring surface inside Console that lets product engineers create region-aware + tier-aware routing rules and configure fallback model variants with built-in validations and an interactive preview matrix. The goal is to make it easy for customers to express common routing intents (prioritize region, prefer lower-cost tier unless latency degrades, fall back to smaller variants) while preventing unsafe configs that could cause request loss or SLO regressions.

Background and motivation:
Customers repeatedly ask for more granular routing control in Console: region pinning, tier prioritization (dedicated vs hosted vs burst), and explicit fallback chains for model variants (e.g., quantized vs full). Currently these are available only via API or YAML. Self-serve teams want a GUI that reduces errors, makes trade-offs explicit, and gives quick simulations so they can validate behavior before saving.

What this ticket delivers:
- An "Authoring Grid" UI in the Routing > Policies page that combines: a region selector, tier ranking control, and a fallback variant matrix.
- Inline validators that check for unreachable rules, circular fallbacks, missing model compatibility (e.g., model A cannot fallback to B if tokenizer mismatch), and capacity-safety warnings when a policy references limited Dedicated pools.
- A Preview panel that runs deterministic simulations on sample traces and displays routing outcomes across axes (region, tier, request size, latency bands).
- Exportable policy JSON and a lightweight lint report explaining warnings and errors.

Design constraints and assumptions:
- Console will reuse existing routing DSL proto from the API; the editor surface maps fields 1:1 to reduce translation errors.
- Preview simulation runs locally in-browser against a small seeded dataset; heavy simulations use a server endpoint (ENG dependency).
- Validation rules come from combined rulebook maintained by runtime and capacity teams (ENG-4218).

UI flows (high level):
1) Start a new routing policy -> choose primary intent (latency-first | cost-first | geo-affinity).
2) Authoring Grid appears with three panels: Regions (multi-select with weights), Tiers (drag-to-rank: Dedicated, Hosted, Burst), Fallback Matrix (rows: primary model variants, cols: fallback candidates with toggle + priority).
3) Save button remains disabled until all critical validations pass; non-critical warnings shown in lint pane.
4) Click "Run Preview" to open a matrix that shows for each sample request which endpoint/model variant would serve it, and estimated latency/cost buckets.

Validation rules (non-exhaustive):
- Error: Circular fallback chains between variants.
- Error: Policy references a dedicated pool that is not in the customer's account.
- Error: Fallback model variant incompatible by tokenizer or input type.
- Warning: Tier ranking places Hosted below Burst while Hosted’s latency SLA is better (cost/latency trade-off).
- Warning: Fallback chain increases expected latency by >40% for majority of sample traces.

Acceptance criteria:
- Customers can create/update routing policies from Console using the Authoring Grid UI and save them to the same schema the API consumes.
- The editor prevents saving when critical validation errors exist and surfaces actionable messages.
- The preview matrix demonstrates routing outcomes for at least 12 seeded traces and shows per-row reason codes (region match, tier fallback, variant fallback).
- Lint report can be downloaded as JSON explaining each validation with severities.
- Console telemetry emits events: policy_created, policy_updated, preview_run, validation_error, validation_warning.

Telemetry and observability:
- Add new console metrics for validation error counts and time-to-fix (user edits after an error).
- Track preview usage to measure whether customers trust the simulator before saving.

Rollout plan and gating:
- Alpha: internal + 3 customer pilots with SEs (two midsize SaaS, one enterprise regulated).
- Beta: open to all customers with a feature flag and opt-in for server-backed simulations.
- GA: enable by default. Security review required prior to GA due to policy export and pool visibility.

API/ENG dependencies:
- ENG-4218: policy validation service (server-backed rules) must expose validation checks and compatibility metadata.
- ENG-4390: preview simulation microservice for larger trace runs (opt-in).
- ENG-4987: permission check endpoints so Console hides dedicated pool options customers cannot use.

Migration and backward-compatibility:
- Authoring Grid will accept legacy YAML imports and attempt to map fields; unsupported constructs surface as warnings and require manual resolution.

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: Customers create overly complex fallback chains that cause high latency. Mitigation: Conservative default warnings and recommended safe templates.
- Risk: Preview results diverge from runtime due to stale capacity metadata. Mitigation: include last-synced timestamp and require server-side validation for critical saves.

Next steps and deliverables for the first sprint:
- UI wireframes and interaction spec (Design).
- Validation rule contract document (Product + Runtime).
- Minimal Console mocks and prototype for in-browser preview.
- Engineering ticket to wire validation API and permission check endpoints.

Links to artifacts:
- Design draft: https://drive.internal.redwood/designs/routing-authoring-grid-v1
- API validation contract: https://confluence.redwood.ai/routing/validation-rulebook-v1
- Pilot sign-up doc: https://docs.internal.redwood/pilot-routing-console
acceptance_criteria: Authoring Grid UI available under Console > Routing > Policies and accessible to customers with routing write permission
Critical validation errors block save; error messages include remediation steps and links to help center
Preview panel shows routing outcome, reason code, and basic latency/cost estimate for seeded traces
Lint report downloadable as JSON that maps to validation IDs used by the backend
Telemetry events emitted for create/update/preview/validation with customer_id and policy_id
